summary: Neo wakes in his dark room lying on his bed and asks if he can go back. Morpheus, sitting 'like a shadow' in a corner, says no and asks whether Neo would want to. Morpheus apologizes, explaining a rule against freeing minds past a certain age because 'They have trouble letting go. Their mind turns against them.' He admits he broke it because he had to. He then recounts the origin myth: a man born inside the Matrix who could remake it, who 'freed the first of us and taught us the truth,' and whom the Oracle prophesied would return to destroy the Matrix and end the war. He says this is why some spend their lives searching for him. Finally Morpheus reveals his motive — 'I believe the search is over' — stands, tells Neo to rest, and when Neo asks 'For what?', answers 'Your training.'

what_changes.before: A newly freed man asking whether there is any return, unsure what he has been drawn into.
what_changes.after: He learns the prophecy of the One and that Morpheus believes 'the search is over,' reframing his own rescue as part of a lifelong quest.
what_changes.evidence: When he died, the Oracle prophesied his return and envisioned that his coming would hail the destruction of the Matrix, an end to the war and freedom for our people. That is why there are those of us that have spent our entire lives searching the Matrix, looking for him.

what_changes.before: An apologetic rule-breaker confessing he endangered Neo by freeing an older mind.
what_changes.after: He steps into the role of mentor and true believer, committing to guide Neo toward 'Your training.'
what_changes.evidence: I did what I did because I believe the search is over.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus confesses why he freed Neo and reveals the prophecy of the One, setting up Neo's training.

minds.wants: To know whether there is any way back to the life he knew — to find a door that is still open.
minds.feels: Raw, emptied, and half-dissolved by what he was shown and by the physical rejection of it (sc-044's collapse). He is not yet ready to be a chosen one; he is a man testing the walls of a trap. But the question is asked from resignation ('Deep down, Neo knows that answer'), so part of him already accepts there is no return and is bracing rather than bargaining.
minds.shows: A single quiet question — 'I can't go back, can I?' — and later one more ('For what?'). He lies still, lets Morpheus talk, and offers no argument against the prophecy.
minds.basis: He opens with 'I can't go back, can I?' rather than a demand to be let out (contrast sc-043/044, where he screamed 'Let me out!' and 'Get this thing out of me!'). The narration says 'Deep down, Neo knows that answer.' His only further line, 'For what?', is passive receptivity, not resistance.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a captor-custodian who has done something irreversible and dangerous to him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is framing himself as a debtor who owes an apology and a guide with a lifelong purpose; he is offering Neo meaning, not merely holding him. Neo has not yet grasped that he is being positioned as the object of a prophecy rather than a victim of an experiment.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's certainty about 'the search is over' is about Neo the person he just woke.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's certainty is about his own faith, not about any verified fact concerning Neo; he is choosing to believe, and will spend the coming events (training, tests) trying to make that belief true.

minds.wants: To reframe what he has done to Neo — a rule-breaking, possibly fatal gamble — as destiny, so that Neo will accept his rescue as purpose rather than trauma and submit to what comes next.
minds.feels: Genuine guilt ('I'm sorry,' 'I broke the rule because I had to') layered over a conviction so total it borders on the devotional. He is steadying himself as much as Neo: the apology is half-confession ('confessing as much to himself as to Neo'), and the myth is the ground he stands on when the ethics of his choice get shaky.
minds.shows: Calm, shadow-still authority. He lets himself show remorse only to immediately transmute it into grandeur — moving from 'dangerous,' 'their mind turns against them,' to the One who will end the war. He withholds the payload ('the search is over') until he is standing and in control of the exit, then closes on 'Your training.'
minds.basis: He sits 'like a shadow' and speaks to the darkness; he explicitly apologizes and explains the age-rule and its danger; he tells the origin myth and the Oracle's prophecy; he ends with 'I believe the search is over' and 'Your training.' The staging — rising only at the reveal — shows deliberate control of the moment.

believes_about.belief: That this broken, frightened man is the One whose coming was prophesied.
believes_about.wrong_because: Unverifiable at this point — it is faith, not knowledge. The coming events (training, the Dojo where Neo is 'brutally beaten,' the rooftop jump he fails) will show Neo as unproven, so Morpheus's certainty is a wager placed ahead of evidence.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready, or will be comforted, to hear that there is no going back because a greater purpose awaits.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo's question is one of loss ('I can't go back, can I?'), not of ambition; Morpheus answers grief with destiny, assuming the trade will satisfy — which Neo has not yet agreed to.

connects_back: Neo's 'I can't go back, can I?' is the exhausted aftermath of sc-043 ('Let me out! I want out!') and sc-044's physical rejection and blackout — the fight has left him, so the question is now resignation, not resistance.
Morpheus's apology for freeing an older mind answers the very rejection just witnessed: Neo's mind and body literally turned against the truth, exactly the danger the rule exists to prevent.
The 'rule we do not free a mind once it reaches a certain age' and 'I broke the rule because I had to' justify the extraction carried out in the power plant (sc-042) and on the main deck (sc-044).
sets_up: ev-010: The prophecy and 'the search is over' frame Neo's rescue as a lifelong quest rather than an accident.
ev-012/ev-013/ev-014: 'Your training' commits Morpheus as mentor and makes the combat, jump, and dojo training the next necessary step.
ev-011: Neo's passive receptivity here sets the baseline against which his lack of physical jacks and his operator orientation will be measured.
dramatic_function: It converts Neo's traumatic, involuntary rescue into a meaningful destiny. By pairing an apology with a myth, Morpheus changes the story from 'you were kidnapped' to 'you were found,' and in doing so pivots the film from revelation into vocation — the moment Neo stops being a victim of the truth and starts being its instrument.
